financials_interim.notes: Single-entity company (Prime Lands Residencies PLC has no subsidiaries reported here; only one column -- 'basis' set to COMPANY as the filing itself uses no Group/Company split). Real-estate developer -- there is no 'trade receivables' line on the balance sheet; trade_receivables is mapped to the closest disclosed line, 'Advances, deposits and other receivables' (152,837,140). 'inventory' = 'Inventory properties' (27,129,912,533), which is unsold/under-construction residential development stock, the core current asset for this business -- not conventional trade inventory. short_term_borrowings = 'Interest bearing borrowings - Current portion' (1,798,808,018) PLUS Bank overdraft (2,712,922,937) = 4,511,730,955, since the overdraft is genuine interest-bearing bank debt for this non-financial company (unlike the bank/NBFI carve-out, which excludes customer deposits, not applicable here). cash_and_equivalents uses the gross Statement of Financial Position 'Cash and cash equivalents' asset line (5,400,004,112), before netting the overdraft (the cash flow statement's netted 'Cash and cash equivalents at the end of the period' figure is 2,687,081,174 after deducting the overdraft -- kept separate here since overdraft is already captured within short_term_borrowings). capex = Acquisition of property, plant and equipment only (25,234,406); smaller items (Rs.1.46mn intangibles, Rs.0.39mn investment property additions) are excluded for consistency with other entries in this DB but together with PPE they reconcile almost exactly to the period's total net investing outflow of 27,081,545.

interim_updates.note_text: Prime Lands Residencies PLC (PLR) revenue nearly doubled YoY, up 98% to Rs.4.59bn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026) from Rs.2.32bn a year earlier, reflecting strong apartment sales handovers/revenue recognition during the quarter. Cost of sales grew even faster in percentage terms (+108%, per the filing's own variance column) than revenue, so gross margin compressed to 26.4% from 29.7% even though gross profit still rose 76% in absolute terms to Rs.1.21bn from Rs.688.2mn. Operating profit rose 92% to Rs.857.1mn from Rs.446.9mn, roughly tracking revenue growth, as distribution expenses (+68% to Rs.183.9mn) and administrative expenses (+30% to Rs.195.1mn) grew much slower than revenue. Below the operating line, finance expenses spiked 509% YoY to Rs.202.7mn from Rs.33.3mn -- a large swing driven by higher loan interest (Rs.141.8mn this quarter per the cash flow statement) and overdraft interest (Rs.56.3mn), consistent with the large increase in both current and non-current interest-bearing borrowings (short-term borrowings roughly Rs.4.51bn including the Rs.2.71bn bank overdraft; long-term borrowings Rs.3.81bn). Finance income also grew 68% to Rs.224.7mn from Rs.133.7mn, partially offsetting the finance cost increase. Net of both, PBT still grew 61% to Rs.879.0mn from Rs.547.2mn, and PAT grew 65% to Rs.661.6mn from Rs.400.5mn, taking basic EPS to Rs.0.71 from Rs.0.43.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for PLR -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. No Group/Company split exists in this filing (single entity, no subsidiaries disclosed), so only one 'COMPANY' basis row is stored. trade_receivables is a best-fit mapping to 'Advances, deposits and other receivables' since the filing has no line explicitly labelled trade receivables (this is a project-based developer that collects customer advances, not conventional trade debtors). diluted EPS left blank -- the filing discloses only a single 'Earnings per share' figure with no explicit statement on dilution (unlike SUN's filing, which explicitly states no dilutive instruments existed).
interim_updates.takeaway: Revenue and profit growth this quarter look very strong (PBT +61%, PAT +65%), but the finance-cost line is the item to watch: finance expenses jumped 509% YoY (Rs.33.3mn to Rs.202.7mn) as the company carries substantially more interest-bearing debt (short-term borrowings including overdraft of ~Rs.4.51bn, long-term borrowings of Rs.3.81bn) to fund its large inventory-properties balance (Rs.27.1bn) -- growth here is increasingly leveraged, and rising finance costs are a genuine risk to monitor even though a matching rise in finance income cushioned the impact this quarter.
operational_highlights: Revenue Rs.4.59bn for Q1 FY2026/27, up 98% YoY from Rs.2.32bn
Gross profit Rs.1.21bn, up 76% YoY; gross margin 26.4% vs 29.7% in the comparative quarter
Operating profit Rs.857.1mn, up 92% YoY, as distribution (+68%) and admin (+30%) costs grew well below revenue growth
Finance expenses spiked 509% YoY to Rs.202.7mn from Rs.33.3mn, driven by higher loan interest (Rs.141.8mn) and overdraft interest (Rs.56.3mn) on a materially larger debt load
Finance income also rose 68% YoY to Rs.224.7mn, partially offsetting the finance cost increase
PBT Rs.879.0mn (+61% YoY), PAT Rs.661.6mn (+65% YoY), basic EPS Rs.0.71 vs Rs.0.43
key_drivers: Strong revenue growth (+98%) reflects a materially higher volume/value of apartment revenue recognised in the quarter versus a year earlier

A large increase in interest-bearing borrowings (short-term incl. overdraft ~Rs.4.51bn, long-term Rs.3.81bn, vs a much smaller base a year earlier) drove the 509% jump in finance expenses to Rs.202.7mn
Inventory properties (unsold/under-construction development stock) of Rs.27.1bn dominate the balance sheet and are the main asset funded by this borrowing

Customer advance collections (a current liability of Rs.13.94bn) fell Rs.812.0mn during the quarter per the cash flow statement, indicating a net drawdown of pre-collected customer deposits as units were completed/handed over

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
